mainTopic: The שפחה חרופה comparisons, and a new משנה on when testimony that a person ate חלב obligates him to bring an offering
overview: The amud opens with רב ששת's objection to a ברייתא that seems to compare things backwards. He explains that with a שפחה חרופה, the פסוק 'שכבת זרע' requires a complete, normal act, so the stronger-looking cases are exempt, just like the weaker ones. The פרק ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה then closes. A new משנה follows about testimony that a person ate חלב: when he brings a חטאת, when he brings an אשם תלוי, and when he is exempt. It includes the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים about two witnesses against his own denial. The משנה also teaches how many offerings are owed for eating forbidden foods in one העלם. The גמרא first reads 'אמרו לו' as two witnesses whom he denies, following רבי מאיר. A second view, using a משנה in יבמות, says 'אמרו' can mean even one witness, and that the case is where he stays silent. Finally the גמרא brings the Torah source, 'או הודע אליו חטאתו', and starts asking which case that ברייתא is about, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The wording seems backwards
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת objects that the ברייתא should have been taught the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have taught the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת hears the ברייתא say 'they made the גומר like the מערה' and says it should have been the reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we say the lighter case is treated like the full case: a מערה, who only begins the act, counts like a גומר, who completes it. Saying the full act is 'like' the partial act sounds strange, because obviously the full act is at least as serious.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite, the reverse
One who completes the act of relations
One who only begins the act (the first stage)

phrases.english: He should have taught the opposite!
phrases.notes: He means it should say 'the מערה is like the גומר', not 'the גומר is like the מערה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the ברייתא the תנא recited just before this point.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the ברייתא: 'עשו גומר כמערה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The usual pattern compares the weaker case to the stronger one, so the comparison here seems reversed.

steps.title: Should the ברייתא be removed?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא asks רב ששת whether he should delete this ברייתא as faulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Should I erase it?
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא who recited the ברייתא asks whether he should take it out completely, since it seems to be wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up רב ששת's next move. Either the ברייתא is a mistake, or there is a way to read it correctly.

keyTerms.meaning: Should I erase or remove it?

phrases.english: He said to him: Should I erase it?
phrases.notes: The תנא who recited the ברייתא is asking רב ששת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the objection by asking whether the text should be deleted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא is faulty and should be removed.

steps.title: With a שפחה חרופה, the full act can be like the partial act
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא is about a שפחה חרופה. There, an unusual completed act is exempt, just like a normal partial act.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. This is what it means: with a שפחה חרופה, they made one who completes an unusual act, for which there is no liability, like one who only begins a normal act. This is because the פסוק says 'שכבת זרע.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת keeps the ברייתא. He explains that it is talking about a שפחה חרופה, where even a completed act done the unusual way brings no liability, just like a partial act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a שפחה חרופה, the תורה says 'שכבת זרע,' so liability needs a complete act done the normal way. An unusual act, even if completed, therefore matches a normal act that was only begun: both are exempt. So the comparison is not backwards. It describes a leniency that applies to this case.

keyTerms.meaning: A maidservant designated (half-betrothed) to a man
In an unusual manner
In the normal manner
'Lying carnally', which shows that a full, normal act is needed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the usual rules of עריות do not automatically carry over to שפחה חרופה, because her פסוק has its own wording.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'like' does not make the lighter case stricter. It makes the heavier case lenient: both cases are exempt.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
this is what it is teaching:
They made one who completes an unusual act
with a designated maidservant, for which they are not liable,
like one who only begins a normal act,
since it is written: 'lies carnally.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers no to deleting the ברייתא and reinterprets it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the ברייתא refers to the special case of שפחה חרופה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא wrongly reversed the usual 'מערה is like גומר' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a שפחה, a completed unusual act is exempt, just like a normal partial act.

steps.title: Two more comparisons for שפחה: intentional and awake
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת continues: with a שפחה, an intentional unusual act is like an unintentional one, and an unusual act done while awake is like one done while asleep. All of these are exempt because of 'שכבת זרע.'
steps.simpleTranslation: One who intends an unusual act with a שפחה, for which they are exempt, is like one who does not intend, since 'שכבת זרע' is written. One who is awake and does an unusual act with a שפחה, for which they are exempt, is like one who is asleep. What is the reason? Since 'שכבת זרע' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת continues his explanation. He reads two more parts of the ברייתא the same lenient way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere, an awake, intentional person is the stricter case. With a שפחה, though, an unusual act brings no liability at all, so it does not matter whether he meant it or was awake. These cases are exempt just like the unintentional or sleeping ones. The same פסוק, 'שכבת זרע,' is the reason each time.

keyTerms.meaning: One who acts on purpose
One who is awake
One who is asleep
They are exempt

phrases.english: One who intends an unusual act with a maidservant,
for which they are exempt, is like one who does not intend,
phrases.notes: 'They' means both the man and the שפחה.

phrases.english: since it is written: 'lies carnally.'
One who is awake doing an unusual act with a maidservant,
for which they are exempt, is like one who is asleep.
What is the reason?
Since it is written: 'lies carnally.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same reinterpretation to the other pairs in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Intentional and awake cases should be the stricter ones.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a שפחה, unusual acts are exempt whether intended or not, and whether awake or asleep.

steps.title: Summary: how שפחה cases line up with other עריות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up: the שפחה cases are like the exempt cases of the other עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes out that one who intends, or one who only begins, with a שפחה is like one who does not intend with all the עריות. One who is asleep doing a normal act is like a sleeper with the עריות. It comes out that one who is awake doing an unusual act with a שפחה is like a sleeper with all the עריות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by matching each שפחה case to the exempt case among the other עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק demands a complete, normal act, the שפחה cases that would be liable with other עריות end up exempt. They count like the unintentional or sleeping cases there. This fully explains the ברייתא's 'reversed' wording.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out, it turns out
The forbidden relationships

steps.whatToRemember: With a שפחה חרופה, the פסוק 'שכבת זרע' requires a complete, normal act. Anything less is exempt, so the ברייתא compares the stronger cases to the weaker ones.

phrases.english: It comes out that one who intends, and one who only begins, with a maidservant
is like one who does not intend with all the forbidden relations.
One who is asleep doing a normal act
is like a sleeper with the forbidden relations.
It comes out that one who is awake doing an unusual act with a maidservant
is like a sleeper with all the forbidden relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes the results of רב ששת's reinterpretation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The שפחה cases match the exempt cases of other עריות, so the ברייתא stays as it is.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of the four who lack atonement
steps.stepSummary: The פרק ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה is formally closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'Four who lack atonement.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line that ends the פרק ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of the שפחה חרופה in the earlier steps finishes the פרק. This line marks the border before a completely new משנה starts.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said when finishing a chapter
People who still lack atonement and must bring an offering before they are fully pure

phrases.english: We will return to you,
chapter 'Four who lack atonement'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek after the conclusion about the שפחה חרופה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה is complete.

steps.title: New משנה: told he ate forbidden fat, he brings a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: If a person is told he ate חלב, he brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If they said to him, 'You ate forbidden fat,' he brings a sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק and a new משנה begin. If someone tells a person that he ate חלב by mistake, he brings a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic is no longer the people who lack atonement. It is now how we know a person sinned. Here he is told he ate חלב and brings a full חטאת. The משנה does not say how he responded, and the גמרא works this out in steps 17–29.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Certain forbidden fats of an animal. Eating them by mistake requires a חטאת
Sin offering, brought for a known accidental sin

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up חֵלֶב (forbidden fat) with חָלָב (milk). They are spelled the same but are completely different things.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If they said to him: You ate forbidden fat,
he brings a sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person told he ate חלב, who accepts it, brings a חטאת.

steps.title: Contradicting witnesses lead to a provisional guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: When one witness says he ate and another says he did not, he brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness says, 'He ate,' and another witness says, 'He did not eat,' or one woman says, 'He ate,' and another woman says, 'He did not eat,' he brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where the witnesses disagree. Since we cannot know if he sinned, he brings an אשם תלוי, the offering for a doubtful sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two equal witnesses who cancel each other leave a real doubt. A doubt about a sin that would require a חטאת calls for an אשם תלוי, not a חטאת. Women are included because in this area a woman's word counts like one witness.

keyTerms.meaning: Provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he did a sin that needs a חטאת
A witness

phrases.english: If a witness says: He ate,
and a witness says: He did not eat,
or a woman says: He ate,
and a woman says: He did not eat,
he brings a provisional guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אוֹמֵר: אָכַל, וְעֵד אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a known sin to a doubtful one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Contradicting single witnesses create a doubt, so he brings an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: One witness against the person's own denial: exempt
steps.stepSummary: If one witness says he ate and he denies it, he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a witness says, 'He ate,' and he says, 'I did not eat,' he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the one witness is contradicted by the person himself. The משנה rules that he does not have to bring anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person knows his own actions better than anyone. So his own denial outweighs a single witness. Unlike step 8, no real doubt remains, so he does not even bring an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt: he has no obligation

phrases.english: If a witness says: He ate,
and he says: I did not eat,
he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אוֹמֵר: אָכַל, וְהוּא אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָכַלְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes who contradicts the witness: now it is the person himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One witness cannot obligate a person who denies the act.

steps.title: Two witnesses against the person's denial: רבי מאיר obligates
steps.stepSummary: When two witnesses say he ate and he denies it, רבי מאיר holds he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two witnesses say, 'He ate,' and he says, 'I did not eat,' רבי מאיר holds him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now makes the testimony stronger by using two witnesses. רבי מאיר says he must bring a חטאת even though he denies it. This sets up the debate that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are a full עדות, which normally decides the facts in court. The question is whether a full עדות can force a person to bring an offering when he insists he never ate.

keyTerms.meaning: Two witnesses: a full, valid testimony
Holds him obligated

phrases.english: If two say: He ate,
and he says: I did not eat,
Rabbi Meir deems him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים: אָכַל, וְהוּא אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָכַלְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises step 9 from one witness to two.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, two witnesses obligate him in a חטאת despite his denial.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's קל וחומר from the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: Two witnesses can sentence a person to death, so surely they can make him bring an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: If two witnesses can bring him to the severe punishment of death, can't they bring him to the lighter matter of an offering?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר proves his ruling. If two witnesses are trusted for a death sentence, they should certainly be trusted for an offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר, a 'how much more so' argument. Two witnesses can override a person's denial even when his life is at stake. So they should be able to override his denial for something much less serious, like a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument: if the strict case works, the lighter case surely does
The severe punishment of death
The lighter matter of an offering

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
If two witnesses can bring him
to the severe punishment of death,
can they not bring him to the lighter matter of an offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִם הֱבִיאוּהוּ שְׁנַיִם לִידֵי מִיתָה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי מאיר's ruling in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's ruling that two witnesses obligate a חטאת against the person's denial.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the power of two witnesses to bring a death sentence.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: he could claim he sinned on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the קל וחומר. He could always say he ate on purpose, and then he would be exempt from an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What if he wants to say, 'I did it on purpose'? Then he would be exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי מאיר's proof. They point out that an offering depends on what the person himself says about his intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is brought only for an accidental sin. Even if the witnesses are right that he ate, he could say 'I did it on purpose' and owe no offering. Since his own word can always exempt him from a קרבן, his denial exempts him too. The death penalty is different, because his word does not control that.

keyTerms.meaning: On purpose. A חטאת is not brought for an intentional sin

steps.whatToRemember: With two witnesses, רבי מאיר obligates a חטאת by a קל וחומר from the death penalty. The חכמים exempt him, because he could always free himself from an offering by saying 'I did it on purpose.'

phrases.english: They said to him:
What if he wishes to say:
'I was acting on purpose'? He would be exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה אִם יִרְצֶה לוֹמַר ״מֵזִיד הָיִיתִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from the death penalty to an offering.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being obligated in an offering depends on the person's own claim about his intent, which witnesses cannot override. A death sentence does not depend on that.

steps.title: Eating forbidden fat twice in one lapse: only one sin offering
steps.stepSummary: Two eatings of חלב in one העלם require only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate forbidden fat and then forbidden fat again, all during one lapse of awareness, he owes only one offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic: how many offerings are owed. Eating the same forbidden food twice without realizing in between counts as one sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An העלם is a stretch of time in which the person doesn't realize he is sinning. If he never 'woke up' between the two eatings, and both are the same kind of food, the eatings join into one sin with one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: One lapse of awareness, with no realization in between
He is liable for only one offering

phrases.english: If he ate forbidden fat and forbidden fat again
in one lapse of awareness,
phrases.notes: Some versions have אַחַת, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is אֶחָד. Both mean 'one.'

phrases.english: he is liable for only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the משנה: counting offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same forbidden food eaten repeatedly in one העלם requires one חטאת.

steps.title: Several different forbidden foods in one lapse: an offering for each
steps.stepSummary: Eating חלב, דם, פיגול and נותר in one העלם requires a separate חטאת for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate forbidden fat, blood, פיגול and נותר, all in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the contrast to step 13. When the forbidden foods are of different kinds, each counts as its own sin, even in one העלם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these foods is a separate prohibition. So they do not join together the way repeated eating of the same food does. One העלם does not merge different prohibitions into one offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood, which is forbidden to eat
A sacrifice made invalid by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten
Sacrificial meat left over past its allowed time
For each and every one

phrases.english: If he ate forbidden fat and blood
and piggul and notar
in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל חֵלֶב וָדָם וּפִיגּוּל וְנוֹתָר בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 13: different types instead of the same type.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different forbidden foods in one העלם each require their own חטאת.

steps.title: Summary: a stringency of many types over one type
steps.stepSummary: The משנה labels the rule of step 14 as a חומר that applies to many מינים and not to one מין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a stringency that applies to many types more than to one type.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up the contrast between steps 13 and 14. Eating several types is stricter, since it brings several offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling this one 'חומר' suggests a list of stringencies. Many types is stricter here, and the משנה will go on to show where one type is stricter instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency, a stricter point
Many types of forbidden food
One type of forbidden food

steps.whatToRemember: One type of forbidden food eaten in one העלם means one חטאת. Different types mean a חטאת for each. That is the חומר of many types over one type.

phrases.english: This is a stringency in many types
over one type.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה חוֹמֶר בְּמִינִין הַרְבֵּה מִמִּין אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the contrast between steps 13 and 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Many types of forbidden food are stricter than one type when it comes to the number of offerings.

steps.title: A stricter rule for one kind: half-olive portions combine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that two half-olive portions eaten in one העלם make a person liable if they are the same kind, but not if they are two different kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a stricter rule for one kind than for many kinds. If he ate half an olive's worth, and then ate another half olive's worth, in one העלם: if both are from one kind, he is liable. If they are from two kinds, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of the comparison from step 15. Here, one kind is stricter than many kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 showed many kinds are stricter, because each kind needs its own חטאת. Here one kind is stricter, because two half-portions of the same kind add up to the full minimum. Two half-portions of different kinds do not join, so no liability results.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of half an olive, which is less than the minimum amount for liability
One kind of forbidden food
Liable to bring an offering
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: Many kinds: stricter, because each kind needs its own חטאת. One kind: stricter, because small amounts add up to a כזית.

phrases.english: And there is a stricter rule for one kind than for many kinds,
that if he ate half an olive's worth
and then went back and ate another half olive's worth
in one period of unawareness,
if from one kind, he is liable,
if from two kinds, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the comparison made in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half-olive portions of one kind combine to make a person liable. Half-olive portions of two kinds do not combine.

steps.title: How many witnesses, and what did the accused answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening case of the משנה. It notes that 'they said' means two witnesses, and asks how the accused responded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches: If they said to him, 'You ate חלב,' he brings a חטאת. 'They said': how many are they? Two. And what did he say to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion with a question about the first case of the משנה. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word 'they said' tells us there are two witnesses. The open question is how the accused reacted, because his reaction may change the law.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה teaches
Two

phrases.english: GEMARA: It teaches:
If they said to him 'You ate forbidden fat,' he brings a sin offering.
'They said': how many are they? Two.
And what did he say to them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins and goes back to the first clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How did the accused respond to the two witnesses: did he stay silent or deny them?

steps.title: First suggestion: he stayed silent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the accused was silent. That reading implies silence before one witness would not make him bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he was silent and did not deny them, then it is only silence before two witnesses that makes him bring a חטאת, but silence before one witness does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer, that he stayed silent. It draws out what that would imply. This prepares the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case were silence before two witnesses, the משנה would be hinting that two are needed. That would mean silence before one witness is not enough for a חטאת. This implication is what the next step attacks.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
He is silent
Denies, contradicts

phrases.english: If you say that he was silent
and did not deny them,
then only silence before two witnesses
is what makes him bring a sin offering,
but for silence before one, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tentative answer: he was silent, which implies silence before one witness is not enough.

steps.title: The middle clause shows silence before one witness is enough
steps.stepSummary: The middle clause exempts him only because he denied the single witness. That implies silence before even one witness makes him liable, which contradicts step 18.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the middle clause: one witness says he ate, and he says, 'I did not eat.' He is exempt only because he denied him. But if he was silent, he would be liable, and all the more so with two witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'he was silent' suggestion using the middle clause of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle clause gives denial as the reason for the exemption, so silence before even one witness would make him liable, and all the more so before two. But step 18 read the first clause as implying that silence before one witness is not enough. The two clauses of the same משנה would contradict each other, so step 18's reading fails.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle clause of the משנה
The reason is
All the more so

phrases.english: Say the middle clause,
one witness says: He ate,
and he says: I did not eat. (He is exempt.)
The reason is that he denies him,
but if he is silent, he is liable,
and all the more so with two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the first clause is about silence before two witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The middle clause implies that silence before one witness already creates liability. That contradicts step 18's inference from the first clause that silence before one witness does not.

steps.title: He denied them, following רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The first clause is about a person who denies two witnesses. It follows רבי מאיר, who holds that denying two witnesses does not count. According to the רבנן he would be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he denies them. Whose view is this? רבי מאיר's, who says that denying two witnesses is not a real denial. But according to the רבנן, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The first clause is about denial, not silence, and it follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he denied two witnesses and still brings a חטאת, the case teaches something new: two witnesses override his denial. That is רבי מאיר's view, stated later in the משנה. The רבנן hold that his own denial exempts him even against two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is it?
A denial of the testimony
The Sages (the majority view)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think everyone holds that denying two witnesses fails. That is only רבי מאיר's view; the רבנן exempt him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the first clause is not a general rule. It is one side of a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and the רבנן.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he denies them,
whose view is it? It is Rabbi Meir's,
who says: a denial of two witnesses
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר says this later in our משנה.

phrases.english: is not a denial,
but according to the Rabbis, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 19 by reading the case as one of denial.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case and assigning it to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause was about silence before two witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is about denying two witnesses and follows רבי מאיר. The רבנן exempt him.

steps.title: Why is the first clause needed if the last clause already teaches it?
steps.stepSummary: If the first clause is about denying two witnesses according to רבי מאיר, the last clause of the משנה already teaches that dispute, so what does the first clause add?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is it teaching us? You can already learn this from the last clause!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 20. If the first clause is about a person who denies two witnesses, it seems to repeat what the last clause already says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גמרא said the first clause follows רבי מאיר, who holds that denying two witnesses does not help. But the last clause of the משנה openly records the argument between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about this exact case. So the first clause looks like an unneeded repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? This asks what new information a statement adds
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
You can learn it from there

phrases.english: And what is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: He means the first clause of the משנה, read the way step 20 explained it.

phrases.english: From the last clause you already learn it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קָמַשְׁמַע לַן? מִסֵּיפָא שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 20 by saying it makes the first clause unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading from step 20, that the first clause is about denying two witnesses according to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה does not repeat itself. If the last clause already teaches רבי מאיר's view on denying two witnesses, the first clause would add nothing.

steps.title: The first clause shows where the dispute applies
steps.stepSummary: The first clause teaches that the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן applies here, in a case where the person contradicts the witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: this matter is the dispute of רבי מאיר and the רבנן, and it is a case where he contradicts them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 21. The first clause is not a pointless repeat. It tells us that this case belongs to the dispute, and that the dispute is about a person who denies the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause, 'they said to him, you ate חלב', does not say how he answered. The גמרא explains that it is teaching us that this case is the argument between רבי מאיר and the רבנן, and that it is talking about a person who denies them (קמכחיש). That way we know the plain ruling 'he brings a חטאת' is only רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us. This gives the new information
A dispute or argument
He contradicts or denies (the witnesses)

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה מַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: this matter is the dispute of רבי מאיר and the רבנן,
and it is a case where he contradicts them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן: דָּבָר זֶה מַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 by giving the first clause its own purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new purpose to the clause: it tells us which case the dispute covers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause seemed to repeat the last clause and teach nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause teaches that this case belongs to the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן, and that he is contradicting the witnesses.
steps.whatToRemember: First approach: 'אמרו לו' means two witnesses, he denies them, and the ruling that he brings a חטאת follows רבי מאיר only.

steps.title: Another view: 'they said' can mean one witness
steps.stepSummary: A second approach says 'אמרו לו' can refer to one witness. It brings support from the משנה about a woman whose husband went overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: 'they said to him' can also refer to one witness. As we learned: a woman whose husband went overseas, and they came and said to her 'your husband died', and she married, and afterward her husband came back, she must leave this one and that one. And we hold that this case is even with one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the problem from steps 18–19. It says the first clause can be about one witness, even though the word 'they said' is plural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first approach began by assuming that the plural 'אמרו' means two witnesses (step 17). This view rejects that starting point: the first clause can be about a single witness. To show that 'they said' can mean one witness, it points to a משנה in יבמות that uses 'they said' for a single witness. How the accused responded is worked out later, in steps 27–29.

keyTerms.meaning: One (here, one witness)
Overseas, a faraway land
She must leave both men
We hold, it is established for us

steps.confusionAlert: Don't be thrown by the plural. 'אמרו' looks like 'they (two) said', but this view shows the משנה can use it even when only one witness spoke.

phrases.english: Some say:
'They said to him' can also be used for one witness,
as we learned:
A woman whose husband went overseas,
and they came and said to her: 'Your husband died,'
and she married, and afterward her husband came back,
she must leave both this one and that one,
and we hold that this is even with one witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: ״אָמְרוּ לוֹ״ נָמֵי חַד קָרֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of the whole discussion. Instead of the first approach (steps 17–22), which assumed 'אמרו' means two witnesses, it reads 'אמרו' as possibly one witness.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the wording: the plural 'אמרו' can refer to a single witness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אמרו לו' was assumed to mean two witnesses, so the first clause could not be about one witness.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אמרו לו' can mean one witness, so the first clause can be about a single witness.
steps.raayaObject: The plural 'אמרו' can be used for one witness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in יבמות about a woman whose husband went overseas, which we hold applies even to one witness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This approach removes the need to say the first clause follows only רבי מאיר.

steps.title: How do we know that case is about one witness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the claim that the משנה in יבמות is talking about one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks how we know the woman's case in יבמות involves only one witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 depends on the claim that 'they said' in the יבמות case means one witness. The גמרא now asks for proof of that claim before relying on it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? What is the source?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the claim in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the first clause of the יבמות משנה is talking about one witness.

steps.title: The last clause of the יבמות משנה shows it
steps.stepSummary: The last clause says that if she married 'without permission', she may go back to her first husband. 'Without permission' means without the court's permission and without relying on one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the fact that the last clause teaches: if she married without permission, she is allowed to go back to him. What does 'without permission' mean? Without permission of the court and without one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 24 by looking at the last clause of the same משנה in יבמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last clause has a woman who married 'without permission', and she may return to her first husband. The גמרא explains that this means she did not need the court's permission based on one witness. In other words, she married on the word of two witnesses. This sets up the contrast for the first clause in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Without permission
Court of Jewish law
She is permitted to return to him
One witness

phrases.english: From the fact that the last clause teaches:
if she married without permission,
she is permitted to return to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is her first husband who came back.

phrases.english: What does 'without permission' mean?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְשׁוּת בֵּית דִּין וְעֵד אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Without the permission of the court and one witness,
phrases.notes: He means she didn't need the court to rely on one witness, because two witnesses testified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 using the last clause of the יבמות משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The last clause, 'without permission', means without the court relying on one witness, so it is a two-witness case.

steps.title: So 'they said' means even one witness
steps.stepSummary: Since the last clause is about two witnesses, the first clause must be about one witness with the court's permission. So 'אמרו' can mean one witness, and the same is true in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that the first clause is with the court's permission and based on one witness. So regarding one witness it says 'they said', and here too, where it says 'they said to him', it means even one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof and applies it to our משנה about חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the last clause in יבמות is about two witnesses, then the first clause, which says 'they came and said', must be about one witness whom the court relied on. So the משנה uses the plural 'אמרו' for one witness. The same can be true for 'אמרו לו' in our משנה, so the first clause can be about a single witness.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies that, by inference
The first clause of a משנה
Evidently, so we see
It means, it implies

steps.whatToRemember: Second approach (איכא דאמרי): 'אמרו לו' can mean one witness, as we see in the משנה in יבמות. So the first clause is about one witness, and a person who stays silent brings a חטאת.

phrases.english: This implies that the first clause
is with the court's permission and based on one witness.
Evidently, about one witness it says 'they said',
and here too, where it says 'they said to him',
it means even one witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא, בִּרְשׁוּת בֵּית דִּין וּבְעֵד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from step 25 and applies it back to our משנה, completing the support for step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The word 'אמרו' can refer to a single witness, so in our משנה 'אמרו לו' can mean one witness.

steps.title: What is the accused person saying? If he denies it, he should be exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the accused person says in the first clause. If he contradicts the witness, how can he bring a חטאת? The middle clause rules that in that case he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the person himself, what is he saying? If you say he contradicts the witness, would he bring a sin offering? But the middle clause teaches: if one witness says 'he ate' and he says 'I did not eat,' he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the first clause of the משנה, which we now read as one witness. It asks how the accused person is reacting, and it tests the first option: that he denies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person denies the one witness, the first clause would say he brings a חטאת. That clashes with the middle clause, which says that when one witness says 'he ate' and he says 'I did not,' he is פטור. So the first clause cannot be about a person who contradicts the witness.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (what is his position)
Contradicts, denies the witness's claim
The middle clause of the משנה
A single witness
Exempt (here, from bringing a חטאת)

phrases.english: And he, what is he saying?
If you say that he contradicts him,
would he bring a sin offering?
But the middle clause teaches:
If one witness says: He ate,
and he says: I did not eat, he is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא, מַאי קָאָמַר? אִלֵּימָא דְּקָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ, מִי מַיְיתֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that 'אמרו' means even one witness, the גמרא tests how the first clause fits with the middle clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the first clause as a case where the accused contradicts the single witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The middle clause says that when one witness is contradicted, the person is פטור. So the first clause cannot make him bring a חטאת in that same case.

steps.title: If he is silent, the first clause is unneeded
steps.stepSummary: The second option: the person is silent. But then the first clause is unneeded, because the middle clause already implies that a silent person is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he is silent. But we can learn that from the middle clause: 'One witness says, etc.' The reason he is exempt is that he contradicts the witness. But if he stayed silent, he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other option, that the accused person stays silent, and shows that this makes the first clause seem unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle clause exempts the person only because he denies the witness. That already tells us that if he is silent, he is חייב. So why would the first clause need to say it? Now both options seem to cause a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Is silent, does not respond
Learn from it, we can infer from it
The reason (that the ruling depends on)
Liable, obligated (here, to bring a חטאת)

phrases.english: Rather, where he is silent,
learn it from the middle clause:
One witness says, etc.
The reason is that he contradicts him,
but if he stayed silent, he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second option of the same dilemma. The first option, that he contradicts, failed. Now the 'silent' option is attacked.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the first clause as a case where the accused is silent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy. The middle clause already implies, by inference, that a silent person is חייב. So the first clause would add nothing.

steps.title: The first clause is about silence, and the middle clause explains it
steps.stepSummary: The first clause really is about a silent person. The middle clause is not a separate ruling. It explains the first clause: this applies only when he is silent, but if he contradicts, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he does not contradict him, and this is what the משנה teaches: If they told him 'you ate חלב,' he brings a sin offering. When is this said? When he is silent. But if he contradicts the witness, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dilemma. The first clause is about a silent person, and the middle clause works as an explanation of the first clause, not as an extra law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the first clause repeats what the middle clause implies. The answer reads them as one unit. The first clause gives the rule, and the middle clause limits it ('when is this said?') to a person who stays silent. Now nothing is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (holding on to an option that was rejected)
And this is what it teaches (rereading the משנה)
In what case are these words said? (adds a limit to a rule)
Forbidden fat, whose eating brings a חטאת if done by mistake
Sin offering brought for an accidental sin

steps.confusionAlert: The middle clause is not a new, separate case here. The גמרא reads it as the explanation ('when is this said?') of the first clause.

phrases.english: Actually, it is where he does not contradict him,
and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אָכַלְתָּ חֵלֶב – מֵבִיא חַטָּאת.
phrases.english: If they said to him: You ate forbidden fat, he brings a sin offering.
In what case is this said? Where he is silent,
but if he contradicts him, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דְּלָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the dilemma of steps 27–28 by rereading how the clauses of the משנה connect.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: the middle clause explains the first clause and is not a separate ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The middle clause was a separate case whose inference made the first clause unneeded.
steps.terutzMaskana: First clause: a silent person is liable even on one witness. Middle clause: this applies only when he is silent, not when he denies.

steps.title: Where in the Torah do we see that a silent person is liable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah-level source that a person who does not deny the witness must bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know, from the Torah, that if he does not contradict the witness he is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know a silent person is liable, the גמרא asks for the Torah source of this rule. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the rule came from reading the משנה. Now the גמרא wants to anchor it in a פסוק. It asks why being told by others, without denying it, makes him bring a חטאת on the Torah level.

keyTerms.meaning: From Torah law
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And from Torah law, from where do we know
that if he does not contradict him, he is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It takes the rule set in step 29 and asks for its Torah source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that makes a silent person liable to a חטאת based on what others tell him.

steps.title: The ברייתא on "או הודע אליו חטאתו"
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא first reads the פסוק as meaning he found out by himself, not through others. Then it reads it as 'in any case': if he does not deny what others tell him, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'Or if his sin is made known to him.' This seems to mean he found out himself, and not that others told him. Might he be exempt even when he does not deny them? The פסוק says 'or if it is made known to him,' meaning in any way he comes to know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that learns from the פסוק that a person told by others is liable, as long as he does not deny it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, "אליו" (to him) sounds like it means he must know it himself, not through others. The ברייתא then asks if that would exempt him even when he doesn't deny it. The words "או הודע אליו" teach that any kind of knowing counts, even through others, as long as he does not deny it.

keyTerms.meaning: Was made known (to him)
One might have thought (a wrong first idea)
The פסוק teaches (to reject that first idea)
In any case, in any way

steps.whatToRemember: In the first clause of the משנה, a person whom even one witness says ate חלב brings a חטאת, as long as he stays silent. If he denies it, he is פטור. The Torah source is "או הודע אליו חטאתו", which means he is liable however he comes to know, even through others.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"Or if his sin is made known to him"
and not that others inform him.
Might it be so even if he does not contradict them?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אוֹ הוֹדַע אֵלָיו״ – מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: The verse states: "Or if it is made known to him," in any case.
phrases.notes: In any way it reaches him, even through other people. Only when he denies it is he exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: אוֹ הוֹדַע אֵלָיו חַטָּאתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question of step 30 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא learns from "או הודע אליו" that a person is liable however he comes to know of his sin, even through others, as long as he does not deny it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a silent person's liability on others' word is a Torah law, not just a rabbinic ruling. This is the basis for the following discussion about how many witnesses the ברייתא means.

steps.title: It cannot be about two witnesses, since that would need no פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא is dealing with. If it means two witnesses told him he sinned and he does not deny it, why would a פסוק be needed? Two witnesses are trusted anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say two witnesses told him, then for two witnesses whom he does not contradict, do we really need a פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 31 by asking which case it is talking about. It tries the first option, two witnesses, and shows that option makes the פסוק pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are a full proof in הלכה. So if he stays silent and does not deny them, it is obvious that they are believed, and the ברייתא would not need a פסוק to teach it. This pushes the גמרא to look for a different case, probably a single witness.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with? A question asking for the exact situation
If you say. It opens a first option that the גמרא will reject
Two, meaning two witnesses, which is a full set of testimony
He contradicts them, meaning he denies what the witnesses say
Does it need a פסוק? A way of saying the law is obvious without one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is doubting the ברייתא's ruling. It agrees that a silent person brings a חטאת. It is only asking which case needs a פסוק to teach this.

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing?
If you say with two witnesses,
two witnesses whom he does not contradict,
is a verse needed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא brought in Step 31 by asking what case its 'in any case' reading could be talking about.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need for a פסוק to teach that a person who does not deny the testimony brings a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case is two witnesses whom he does not deny, they are a full testimony and are obviously believed. So the פסוק would teach nothing new.
